petty-troubles-of-married-life-second-pa: Honoré de Balzac turns his unsparing eye on marriage in these satirical sketches — the second half of his comic anatomy of wedded life. Husbands and wives maneuver, misunderstand, and exasperate each other in scenes any married reader will recognize. Balzac's wit is sharp but affectionate: he laughs at marriage because he finds it endlessly, fascinatingly human.
the-clicking-of-cuthbert: Wodehouse turns to golf in this collection of linked comic tales from the clubhouse. The Oldest Member spins yarns of duffers in love, matches won and lost, and the strange power of the game. Even non-golfers will laugh — the master is at his most infectious.
at-agincourt: Henty's boy hero fights at Agincourt beside Henry V — the longbowmen, the mud of the field, the glorious victory against fearful odds. Young readers march through one of England's proudest days, learning history with every charge. Thrilling, instructive, and pure Henty.
the-rising-of-the-court: Henry Lawson's Rising of the Court — bush ballads and stories of shearing sheds, selections, and outback justice — gave Australia its own voice. His verses of swagmen and battlers made him the people's poet. The essential Lawson for all lovers of the bush.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adalbert: This 1913 reference piece on St. Adalbert — the apostle of Prussia, martyred in 997. F.M. Rudge tells his missionary tale. Prague's bishop died for the northern pagans. Poland's patron wears his crown of thorns.
